xAoljeRJ3lU.summary: SciPy 2015 talk by Nathaniel Smith and Stefan van der Walt on choosing a new default colormap for Matplotlib. It covers why Jet misleads, how perceptual color spaces work, and how viridis was designed.
xAoljeRJ3lU.why: HN's go-to recommendation for colormap and color-perception questions; commenters call it funny, brief, clear and a favorite talk.

xguam0TKMw8.summary: An animated 44-minute summary of Ray Dalio's book Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order. It lays out the Big Cycle of rising and declining nations, covering debt cycles, internal conflict, and shifts in global power over the past 500 years.
xguam0TKMw8.why: HN commenters recommend it as a clear framework for placing the current US and world situation within historical debt and empire cycles.

x1bX3F7uTrg.summary: A three-minute parody of Adam Curtis's documentary style, assembled from archive footage with his typical narration and leaps of logic.
x1bX3F7uTrg.why: Recommended as the standard companion to any Adam Curtis film, since it lampoons the style and gives reasons to take his claims with skepticism.

xOCurBYI_gY.summary: Tom7 explains and demos software that learns to play NES games by finding score patterns in memory and then searching for inputs that raise it. It is the video companion to his SIGBOVIK paper.
xOCurBYI_gY.why: Loved on HN as a hilarious, brilliant example of hacker-academic work and cited whenever game-playing AI or fuzzing comes up.

x7cQ3mrcKaY.summary: Pete Hunt of Facebook and Instagram introduces React at JSConf EU 2013 and explains its design principles. He argues that separating templates from logic only separates technologies, not concerns, and makes the case for components.
x7cQ3mrcKaY.why: HN calls it the famous talk for understanding why React rejected separation of concerns by technology and for newcomers puzzled by JSX.

xsSnOQynTHs.summary: Dan Abramov live-codes hot reloading with time-travel debugging at React Europe 2015, debuting Redux and its devtools. The slides themselves are driven by application state.
xsSnOQynTHs.why: Seen as the canonical Redux introduction and a model live-coding talk about better developer tools.

xx7Lfh5SKUQ.summary: Michael Steil and Christian Hessmann's 34C3 talk explaining the Apollo Guidance Computer end to end: hardware design, operating system, and mission software.
xx7Lfh5SKUQ.why: Repeatedly called the best and most comprehensive AGC talk, with commenters rewatching it and treating it as foundational computer architecture learning.

xt1KNDmOYqA.summary: Casey Muratori argues against smart pointers and RAII, advocating grouped-element thinking, zero-is-initialization and stubs as better ways to structure memory and handle errors.
xt1KNDmOYqA.why: HN commenters in memory management and language design threads cite it as the best explanation of group lifetimes versus per-object ownership.

xP5-iIeKXE8.summary: A two-minute video of Conway's Game of Life running inside Conway's Game of Life, built from OTCA metapixels and Golly. It zooms smoothly between scales.
xP5-iIeKXE8.why: The canonical visual for nested simulation, Turing completeness and self-reference; HN readers call it mind-blowing and reach for it constantly.

x2H60ritjag.summary: Soil microbiologist Elaine Ingham speaks at the Oxford Real Farming Conference on how soil organisms cycle nutrients, unlock minerals from rock and air, and why pesticides and fertilizers harm soil life. Slides are linked in the description.
x2H60ritjag.why: HN commenters cite her as the explanation for why soil biology, not added fertilizer, drives plant nutrition and farm results.

xtpgkX588nM.summary: A 1968 Firing Line interview in which Milton Friedman explains the negative income tax, a proposal to replace welfare bureaucracy with direct payments.
xtpgkX588nM.why: The go-to primary source in basic income threads for Friedman's negative income tax idea.

xRel1JKOEbI.summary: Neuroscientist Anil Seth gives a Royal Institution lecture on the science of consciousness. He separates conscious level, content and self, and argues that experience arises from the brain's predictive inference.
xRel1JKOEbI.why: HN commenters recommend it as a clear, in-depth lecture on consciousness as a process of prediction.

xoVJKj8lcNQ.summary: Tristan Harris and Aza Raskin of the Center for Humane Technology present why current AI capabilities pose catastrophic societal risks. They argue companies are racing to deploy without adequate safety, and that institutions must adapt. It was given before GPT-4's launch.
xoVJKj8lcNQ.why: Frequently recommended as the overview to get up to speed on AI risk, especially by people who valued The Social Dilemma.

xMP_AfiNlX4.summary: First of an 18-part lecture series by engineer Dan Gelbart on building prototypes. The series covers practical mechanical design and fabrication of precision machines.
xMP_AfiNlX4.why: Recommended as a gold-standard free course for anyone learning to build precision mechanical things.

xSGx3HSjKDo.summary: A short BicycleDutch episode showing how people with disabilities use Dutch cycle tracks on hand-cycles, tricycles and mobility scooters.
xSGx3HSjKDo.why: HN cites it to show that cycling infrastructure also serves disabled and mobility-impaired people.

xe-f4gokRBs.summary: Smarter Every Day films Prince Rupert's drops, tempered glass drops, in high-speed slow motion at 130,000 fps. It shows how the drop's heavy internal stress lets the head survive hits while the tail shatters the whole thing.
xe-f4gokRBs.why: Recommended across Prince Rupert's drop and glass threads for its striking high-speed footage.

xixM_cwSLcQ.summary: A Boeing 737 pilot explains the runaway stabilizer checklist, the procedure for stopping unwanted horizontal stabilizer movement such as an MCAS activation on the 737 MAX. He walks through the steps, the trim cutout switches and the jackscrew mechanism, and shows a simulator run including the manual trim wheel effort.
xixM_cwSLcQ.why: During the 737 MAX crash coverage, HN commenters linked it as a clear, pilot-led demonstration of what an MCAS runaway looks like and how hard manual trim is to crank.

xrIjfIjssLE.summary: A short Ericsson film demoing Erlang, showing concurrent processes, debugging tools, and hot code reloading, including crashing parts of a running system while calls continue.
xrIjfIjssLE.why: A beloved classic that HN recommends as the quickest way to see why Erlang is special.

xzYgiOC9cj4.summary: An 11-minute clip of Milton Friedman explaining the incentives of unions and how they affect employment. He argues unions restrict labor supply, raising pay for some workers while hurting low-skill workers.
xzYgiOC9cj4.why: HN commenters share it in union threads as a concise statement of the free-market economist's case against unions.

x5Efg42-Qn0.summary: Todd Becker's Ancestral Health Symposium talk arguing that myopia is driven by near-work and can be reversed, covering the biology and epidemiology and experimental evidence for reversal by using weaker lenses.
x5Efg42-Qn0.why: HN commenters credit it as a life-changing talk, with some reporting reduced prescriptions after following the method.

xKu2de0yCJI.summary: The 1969 pitch film in which Saul Bass presents the Bell System logo redesign to AT&T, part of the largest corporate re-identity program in U.S. history.
xKu2de0yCJI.why: HN holds it up as a masterclass in explaining and selling a design.

xnez6tloNSQ.summary: Redis Labs and Tim Davis present RedisGraph, which uses GraphBLAS to treat graph queries in Cypher as sparse linear algebra for lower latency.
xnez6tloNSQ.why: Recommended in graph database threads as a mind-blowing case for expressing graph analysis as linear algebra.

x1v2tX4_dkQ.summary: Christof Paar's university lecture introducing Galois fields and finite-field arithmetic as used in AES. It covers the mathematics behind the AES S-box.
x1v2tX4_dkQ.why: Recommended as a moderately formal, clear introduction to finite fields, useful beyond AES.

x7drE24geUw.summary: Martin Kleppmann surveys current research on CRDTs, the algorithms for merging concurrent edits across offline replicas. He covers the hard parts such as rich text, moves and merge results that are technically correct but poor.
x7drE24geUw.why: Recommended as an excellent first education on CRDTs and their limits.

xLEe496IS1o.summary: Part one of Errol Morris's First Person interview with Murray Richman, a New York lawyer who defends mob figures. He talks about how he sees the law and his clients.
xLEe496IS1o.why: HN recommends it as the best interview of Morris's series and as an insight into how the law and ordinary people's minds work.

xNjI03CGkb4.summary: A 2016 conference talk by a mobile game CEO on the tricks of free-to-play monetization, including player profiles and how to target high-spending whales.
xNjI03CGkb4.why: HN mostly cites it critically, as an insider's blunt playbook for psychologically exploiting players in F2P and loot box games.

xNzoerDljjo.summary: Sasa Juric explains how to parse a language from first principles without regexes, live-coding a simple parser combinator library in Elixir. It was given at WebCamp Zagreb 2019.
xNzoerDljjo.why: HN commenters recommend it as a clear, dense hour on parsers and parser combinators that holds the audience.

xi1Lq79mLeE.summary: Dave Plummer interviews Dave Cutler, architect of VMS and Windows NT, in a roughly three-hour conversation about his career and the history of Windows.
xi1Lq79mLeE.why: Recommended as a long, excellent first-hand interview with a legendary OS designer, though some note it is light on technical detail.

xoxhDk-hwuo.summary: Mark Rober builds a glitter-bomb booby-trapped package to take revenge on porch pirates, filming the thieves' reactions. Some reactions were later acknowledged as partially staged.
xoxhDk-hwuo.why: Linked as the funny, famous porch-pirate revenge video whenever package theft comes up, with the faked-reactions caveat noted.

x2-rSnhpw0g.summary: Simon Brown's Agile on the Beach 2019 talk presents the C4 model, a lightweight approach to diagramming software architecture with a shared vocabulary and simple notation.
x2-rSnhpw0g.why: Recommended as the introduction to C4 when people ask how to visualize and communicate software architecture.

x94PGgYKHQ0.summary: FortNine's tongue-in-cheek guide to why drivers fail to see motorcyclists and how riders can make themselves more visible. It touches on perception psychology, including the role of saccades.
x94PGgYKHQ0.why: Cited in threads on motorcycle and cyclist safety to explain why drivers look and still miss them.

xLYYh4aPXAM.summary: A Reason TV segment, drawing on Alex Gladstein of the Human Rights Foundation, argues that Bitcoin works as an escape hatch for people living under authoritarian governments and inflating currencies.
xLYYh4aPXAM.why: HN commenters use it in crypto debates as evidence that Bitcoin matters for people in unstable-currency countries.

xMzojQFyMo0.summary: A short vintage film clip of Seymour Papert, creator of Logo, on using computers to spark children's imagination and learning.
xMzojQFyMo0.why: Recommended as a glimpse of Papert's vision of computers as tools for learning, shared especially after his death.

xbBdIG--b58.summary: Permaculture instructor Andrew Millison travels with the UN World Food Programme to Niger to see land recovery within the Great Green Wall, where rainwater harvesting is boosting food security and restoring the ecosystem.
xbBdIG--b58.why: Recommended in regreening and desertification threads as an optimistic, constructive example of land restoration.

xnWKz7Cthkk.summary: Top Gear episode in which Jeremy Clarkson and team try to destroy a Toyota Hilux pickup through water, fire, and a demolished building. It is the first part of the 'Killing a Toyota' series.
xnWKz7Cthkk.why: HN uses it as the go-to evidence for Toyota pickup durability, and as a benchmark in discussions of truck toughness.

xodtfM1r9FA.summary: The first of an eight-part ScienceClic series building general relativity, covering worldlines, proper time and coordinate systems with animated visualizations.
xodtfM1r9FA.why: Praised for its visualizations and pedagogy in threads about physics and differential geometry.

xsLJZyih3Ac.summary: Mark Rober and collaborators build glitter bomb traps and other pranks to fight phone scam call centers, and share evidence about the operations.
xsLJZyih3Ac.why: Offered as a satisfying example of fighting back against scam call centers.

xtvT2XYlcOY.summary: Coverage of the McMurtry Speirling fan car breaking the Goodwood hillclimb record with a 39.08 second run driven by Max Chilton. It beat the Volkswagen ID.R and the 1999 McLaren time.
xtvT2XYlcOY.why: Shared as a striking example of a fan car using powered ground effect, with an eye-popping launch, in EV and motorsport threads.

xuCn8ux2gbs.summary: A fast, absurdist 19-minute animated run through the history of the whole world, narrated and scored by Bill Wurtz in his distinctive style. It compresses millennia of events into jokes, songs and quick visuals.
xuCn8ux2gbs.why: HN commenters list it among favorite long-form, info-dense YouTube videos and as a representative piece of Wurtz's quirky creativity.

xGbgDf4HCHU.summary: A 2020 UC San Diego event with Roger Penrose and Stuart Hameroff presenting their Orch OR theory that consciousness arises from quantum processes in brain microtubules, followed by a conversation with Roger Bingham.
xGbgDf4HCHU.why: HN commenters point to it as a presentation of the Penrose-Hameroff theory of consciousness, which some find compelling.

xL_sMXfzzyA.summary: A 1952 filmed interview in which Romney Wheeler talks with philosopher Bertrand Russell at his home in Surrey. Russell discusses his outlook and reflects on how the world changed over the first half of the century.
xL_sMXfzzyA.why: HN users share it as a chance to hear Russell speak himself and get a sense of his values and outlook.

xMabpBvtXr4.summary: An Innuendo Studios video essay from the Alt-Right Playbook series that uses the Seinfeld 'the card says moops' scene to explain bad-faith argument tactics. It describes how reactionaries use sincerity and irony as shields in online debate.
xMabpBvtXr4.why: HN commenters recommend the series for understanding bad-faith 'just kidding' dynamics and trolling online.

xR7XMkjDGw0.summary: A short clip of George R.R. Martin asking Stephen King on stage how he writes so fast. King describes setting daily page goals, around six pages a day, and keeping focused hours.
xR7XMkjDGw0.why: Shared in productivity and writing threads for King's simple daily-quota approach to producing a lot of work.

xUezfuy8Qpc.summary: Rowan Atkinson speaks against the word 'insulting' in the UK Public Order Act, as part of the Reform Section 5 campaign. He argues for robust free speech and against the slippery slope of criminalizing offense.
xUezfuy8Qpc.why: HN commenters point to it as an eloquent defense of free speech with concrete examples of the slippery slope.

xY45YE7ggng.summary: Brian Troutwine's Code Mesh 2015 talk on the Apollo Guidance Computer. It covers the AGC's design, core rope memory, its interrupt and software behavior, and the pioneering engineering effort behind it.
xY45YE7ggng.why: Recommended as a wonderful overview of the AGC architecture, though one commenter found it uninspiring.

xYemnKEKx0c.summary: Jon Ronson, author of The Psychopath Test, gives a TED talk on the blurry line between sane and crazy and on psychopathy as a spectrum, with stories of how the label gets applied.
xYemnKEKx0c.why: Praised as one of the great non-technical talks, appearing in best-talk lists.

x_q50tvbQm4.summary: A 1984 Computer Chronicles segment in which Susan Kare explains the ergonomics and interface design of the original Macintosh. She introduces the interface step by step for newcomers.
x_q50tvbQm4.why: Praised as a lesson in explaining technology to non-technical people and as a window into early Mac design.

xb8idEf-Iak.summary: A 1993 interview in which Steve Jobs talks about designer Paul Rand, who created the NeXT logo. He recounts Rand's insistence on presenting a single design and his uncompromising professionalism.
xb8idEf-Iak.why: HN commenters share it for Jobs's account of Rand's single-option approach and as a lesson in trusting designers.

xcwJt4bcnXs.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on cities spending public money on privately owned sports stadiums, including how tax-exempt municipal bonds subsidize them.
xcwJt4bcnXs.why: Pointed to in debates over stadium subsidies as a persuasive case that cities should not pay for stadiums.

x-rJciYZmi0.summary: Michael Green of Thiel Macro presents a thesis that the growth of passive investing distorts how markets price new money flows. He ties short-term market behavior to longer-term demographic cycles and its effects on valuations and volatility.
x-rJciYZmi0.why: HN points to it in investing threads as an argument that passive index flows distort markets and could precede a crash.

x6AOwDttBsc.summary: Tested gets hands-on with four Meta Reality Labs research VR headset prototypes testing resolution, brightness, focus shifting and form factor, plus an interview with Mark Zuckerberg on display technology.
x6AOwDttBsc.why: Recommended as a detailed, level-headed look at the technical challenges Meta faces in VR.

xEDZQtAHpX8.summary: Markus Winand shows how SQL has evolved since SQL-92, comparing old-style solutions to modern features such as window functions and system versioning, and notes that many developers never learn them.
xEDZQtAHpX8.why: Recommended as the best introduction to modern SQL standard features that textbooks skip.

xFFs9UgOAlE.summary: A December 2005 guest lecture by Mark Zuckerberg in Harvard's CS50, discussing Facebook's early days, its technical choices and computer science. It captures him as a 21-year-old founder before Facebook's rise.
xFFs9UgOAlE.why: HN commenters mine it for early-Facebook history, such as his view on open source, privacy and the problems that shaped its architecture.

xFKFoGiGlXQ.summary: Kaze Emanuar searches for the best sine approximation for the Nintendo 64, comparing the lookup tables in Mario 64 and Ocarina of Time with polynomial alternatives. It walks through numerics and 3rd, 4th and 5th order approximations.
xFKFoGiGlXQ.why: Cited in discussions of sine implementations and whether lookup tables beat computation on memory-bound hardware.

xJ6Ym719urg.summary: A long Joe Rogan Experience interview with mycologist Paul Stamets about fungi, medicinal mushrooms and bioremediation.
xJ6Ym719urg.why: HN commenters recommend it as a long, engaging introduction to Stamets and his fungi work.

xMYm2d9bmEA.summary: Musician Benn Jordan explains and demonstrates adversarial noise that poison-pills music files against AI training and scraping.
xMYm2d9bmEA.why: HN points to it in AI music and data-poisoning threads as the source for this technique.

xVodkE47aLw.summary: An episode of the Well There's Your Problem podcast on five-over-one buildings, wood-frame floors atop concrete bases, with engineering background and some oil industry news. It is long, rambling and has NSFW language.
xVodkE47aLw.why: Recommended in housing and architecture threads for its engineers' critique of five-over-one construction.

xZi4kTJG-LE.summary: Tyler Bosmeny, CEO of Clever, gives a Y Combinator Startup School talk on how early-stage companies should approach sales and build an enterprise sales team.
xZi4kTJG-LE.why: Recommended to technical founders who need a practical introduction to B2B and enterprise sales.

x_yHtfGH0nI.summary: An Engineering Giants documentary episode following a British Airways Boeing 747-400 through a D-check, the heaviest maintenance inspection, in Cardiff. The aircraft is stripped down and inspected nearly everywhere.
x_yHtfGH0nI.why: Recommended as a great look at how thoroughly airliners are inspected and rebuilt, and cited in aviation maintenance discussions.

xa2Kpkksf3k.summary: PBS Space Time examines Roger Penrose's idea that consciousness arises from quantum processes in the brain, and reviews new evidence about microtubules. It ends with an estimate of what replicating consciousness would demand.
xa2Kpkksf3k.why: Pointed to as a clear, balanced overview of quantum-brain theories when AI consciousness and brain models come up.

xb_PyKuI7II.summary: A Hitachi promotional cartoon in the style of Schoolhouse Rock explaining perpendicular magnetic recording for hard drives.
xb_PyKuI7II.why: Remembered fondly as a fun, memorable animated explanation of how perpendicular disk storage works.

xc8epam4NyY.summary: A short clip of comedian David Mitchell on The Last Leg discussing tax avoidance versus tax evasion and why taxes matter.
xc8epam4NyY.why: Cited as a witty, clear take on the avoidance versus evasion distinction.

xdfeXqHFmPI.summary: A one-minute scene from The Gambler in which John Goodman's loan shark explains the 'position of f you': having enough money to walk away from any employer or deal.
xdfeXqHFmPI.why: HN links it whenever the discussion turns to layoffs, saving, and having enough financial independence to say no.

xg29TuWo0Yo.summary: An Adult Swim fake infomercial in which Alan Resnick pitches a four-step program for creating a digital avatar to live forever. It is absurdist satire of tech immortality and digital popularity.
xg29TuWo0Yo.why: HN commenters point to it as satire that illuminates strange transhumanist and digital immortality culture.

xn76r0JxqNM.summary: A HandmadeCon 2016 panel where Chris Hecker, John Miles, Sean Barrett and Chris Green give an oral history of software texture mapping in 90s games.
xn76r0JxqNM.why: HN recommends it for first-hand accounts of how early 3D games like Doom worked within tight hardware limits.

xnqTKD8uD64.summary: Herb Sutter revisits basic C++ questions in light of C++11 and C++14: how to declare and initialize variables, pass values to functions, write loops, and use smart pointers. It covers auto, rvalue references, range-for, uniform initialization, lambdas, unique_ptr and shared_ptr.
xnqTKD8uD64.why: HN people list it among the go-to talks for learning or refreshing modern C++ style, and cite it for Sutter's guidance on function parameter passing.

x1SgmFa0r04.summary: A short NASA Goddard visualization from the GEOS-5 model showing a year of atmospheric carbon dioxide moving around the globe. It shows plumes from sources, hemispheric differences and seasonal swings as plants grow and die back.
x1SgmFa0r04.why: HN commenters use it as a vivid illustration of how CO2 is distributed and how vegetation absorbs it seasonally.

xZePwin92cI.summary: A 1951 Bell System training film showing how telephone calls are routed through a step-by-step (Strowger) switching office.
xZePwin92cI.why: HN uses it as a favorite old explainer for mechanical telephone switching.

x1H-323d838.summary: NileRed attempts to make transparent wood, inspired by an AvE video, by removing lignin and infiltrating the wood with resin. It is a long, detailed walkthrough of the chemistry and the practical difficulties.
x1H-323d838.why: Linked as the go-to hands-on demonstration of how transparent wood is made and why scaling it to large pieces is hard.

x7qPAY9JqE4.summary: Steve Jobs's January 2007 MacWorld keynote segment introducing the original iPhone. He presents it as a widescreen iPod, a phone and an internet communicator in one device.
x7qPAY9JqE4.why: HN commenters cite it as a model of a clear product reveal and as the source for how Jobs framed the iPhone's three functions and dismissed physical keyboards.

x85342Cny8c.summary: A Google talk from the Chisel community in which engineers recount designing the Edge TPU with the Chisel hardware construction language. It covers the productivity gains and the problems they hit.
x85342Cny8c.why: Pointed to as a rare first-hand account of a real, shipping ASIC built in an open-source HDL, useful in HDL and FPGA choice discussions.

x8TO-nrUtSI.summary: Modern Vintage Gamer explains why PlayStation 1 graphics warped and jittered, comparing it with the Nintendo 64. The causes are affine texture mapping and the lack of sub-pixel vertex precision.
x8TO-nrUtSI.why: Used as the accessible explanation of PS1 rendering quirks whenever retro 3D graphics or PS1-style renderers come up.

xGQxSJmadm0.summary: Chris Boden shows how an operator starts a large hydroelectric turbine generator and manually synchronizes it to the grid using a needle phase meter.
xGQxSJmadm0.why: HN links it in power grid threads as a concrete demonstration of generator synchronization.

xK4MBzp5YwM.summary: A short documentary on the 2015 Yale Halloween costume controversy and the confrontation with Nicholas Christakis. Filmmaker Rob Montz investigates campus free speech and the state of the university afterward.
xK4MBzp5YwM.why: Cited in debates about campus culture, free speech and workplace diversity controversies as a window into a particular mindset.

xKCuDxpccYM.summary: Elon Musk gives students at the Sorbonne a short, simple explanation of climate change and carbon emissions shortly before the 2015 COP21 conference in Paris. He covers why CO2 accumulation matters and argues for a carbon tax.
xKCuDxpccYM.why: Cited as evidence that Musk has long taken climate change seriously and as a concise statement of his views on carbon pricing.

xQ3oJlt4GrI.summary: Dave Jones of EEVblog tears down a 1991 IBM 9121 thermal conduction module from a System/390 mainframe, a 63-layer ceramic hybrid module with 2772 pins worth about $250,000, and demonstrates a BGA desoldering technique.
xQ3oJlt4GrI.why: Cited in threads on chip packaging and cooling as a vivid look at vintage IBM mainframe module construction.

xQbaVdge7kU.summary: Practical Engineering explains how engineers and agencies put a dollar value on a human life to weigh cost against safety. It covers the legal and regulatory basis for these calculations.
xQbaVdge7kU.why: HN commenters cite it as an interesting look at valuing human life, used in safety and liability discussions.

xQx-tuW9A4Q.summary: A Talks at Google visit by Douglas Engelbart, inventor of the mouse. He presents his lifelong aim of augmenting collective human intelligence, followed by a Q&A.
xQx-tuW9A4Q.why: Recommended for hearing Engelbart's vision of collaborative hypertext systems straight from him, including his view of Wikipedia.

x_JCBmY9NGM.summary: A stand-up routine by Stewart Lee on political correctness, offering a satirical defense of inclusive language.
x_JCBmY9NGM.why: HN quotes and links it as a witty take on political correctness in culture-war and language threads.

xgKY9hmbfgo.summary: EmpLemon examines Nintendo's brand-protection strategy, its aggressive legal actions and its relationship with fans and creators.
xgKY9hmbfgo.why: Pointed to in threads about Nintendo lawsuits and takedowns as an explanation of how the company behaves.

xjEFo3a1AnI.summary: Andrew Huberman interviews Harvard psychiatrist Chris Palmer about nutrition, metabolism and mental health, including the ketogenic diet as a treatment for depression and schizophrenia.
xjEFo3a1AnI.why: Cited in threads on metabolism and mental illness, especially keto for psychiatric conditions.

xqGAC5QCYuQ.summary: A Rubber Duck Engineering episode on the years before Flutter, covering web projects and three JavaScript frameworks that influenced it, and the early DOM-based, network-loaded Flutter.
xqGAC5QCYuQ.why: Recommended as an insider account of how Flutter came to be and why it chose Dart.

xwA4k0E51Oo.summary: A PBS NewsHour report on a viral compilation of local TV anchors reading identical scripts, which raised concerns about Sinclair Broadcasting mixing partisan opinion into local news. It also covers Sinclair's reach and its bid to grow larger.
xwA4k0E51Oo.why: Cited as a short, concrete example of consolidated media ownership pushing coordinated messaging through local news.

xzjqjU2FOwA.summary: Eric Weinstein interviews economist Timur Kuran on The Portal about preference falsification and how societies where people hide their real views can tip into revolutions.
xzjqjU2FOwA.why: Pointed to as a good explanation of preference falsification and its effects on speech and politics.

x-5zEb1oS9A.summary: A classic Yes, Minister sketch in which the Minister visits a brand-new, fully staffed hospital with no patients and demands that some be found.
x-5zEb1oS9A.why: Used as a joke for bureaucracy that exists to employ administrators rather than serve its purpose.

x034jVB1avs.summary: Brandon Thomas demos Laser Pong, a game he built on a laser projector and projected onto buildings around Atlanta. It was a weekend project.
x034jVB1avs.why: Cited by HN as a fun example of a laser projector side project that later led to jobs and wealth for its author.

x0YGZPycMEU.summary: The Little Britain sketch in which call-center worker Carol types into her computer and replies 'computer says no' to every request.
x0YGZPycMEU.why: HN uses it as a joke reference to automated systems and bureaucratic refusals.

x2ZLS1V3iMw.summary: A one-minute Telegraph news clip of Cristiano Ronaldo moving two Coca-Cola bottles aside at a Euro 2020 press conference and saying 'Drink water.' The moment went viral and drew praise from anti-obesity campaigners.
x2ZLS1V3iMw.why: Cited in threads about sugary drinks, alcohol and advertising as a famous example of a star publicly rejecting a sponsor's product.

x73PkUvArJY.summary: A short stand-up clip from James Acaster's Netflix special about the British Empire and museums that display things taken from other countries in glass boxes.
x73PkUvArJY.why: HN cites it jokingly in threads about repatriating stolen artifacts and the British Museum.

x7MvtQp2-UA.summary: A short Great Big Story piece on the Ocracoke Brogue, or Hoi Toider dialect, spoken on North Carolina's Outer Banks, which developed through centuries of isolation and traces back to the 1600s.
x7MvtQp2-UA.why: Linked as an audio example of the Ocracoke accent in threads about American dialects.

x7psGHgatGM.summary: Ali Rahimi accepts the NIPS 2017 Test of Time Award and argues that machine learning has become alchemy, with practice running ahead of understanding.
x7psGHgatGM.why: Cited when HN discusses the lack of rigor and theory in deep learning, often with a pointer to the key moment of the talk.

xA4QWwaweWA.summary: A short IBM behind-the-scenes documentary on how researchers moved individual atoms to make the world's smallest movie. It introduces the scientists and their work on atomic memory and data storage.
xA4QWwaweWA.why: HN commenters link it as the making-of companion to IBM's atom stop-motion film.

xAUJYP8tnRE.summary: Kurzgesagt animated explainer on the Dark Forest answer to the Fermi Paradox. It argues that if advanced civilizations exist, staying silent may be the safest strategy because revealing yourself invites a first strike.
xAUJYP8tnRE.why: HN commenters cite it as the accessible summary of the Dark Forest theory whenever SETI, alien contact, or hostile-environment analogies come up.

xAxtxPAUcwQ.summary: A one-minute 1999 Qwest commercial where a hotel clerk promises every movie ever made in any language, any time.
xAxtxPAUcwQ.why: HN uses it as a nostalgic example of the promised any-media-on-demand future that never fully arrived.

xC5uEe5OzNQ.summary: A 2007 side-by-side demo comparing Windows Vista's Aero interface with Ubuntu running Beryl/Compiz, showing effects such as the desktop cube and burning windows.
xC5uEe5OzNQ.why: HN commenters cite it as the widely seen nostalgic video from the era when Linux desktop effects outpaced Vista.

xDcvPf78g1k.summary: Highlight clip from the 2021 Free Expression Awards honoring YouTube CEO Susan Wojcicki. The video became notable for its overwhelmingly negative like/dislike ratio.
xDcvPf78g1k.why: Cited as an ironic example of YouTube receiving a free expression award, and as a showcase of the public dislike count before it was hidden.

xH_6_8NOfwI.summary: A two-minute scene from The Wire in which Baltimore police brass pressure subordinates to fix the crime statistics. It dramatizes how metrics and incentives distort policing.
xH_6_8NOfwI.why: Used as a shorthand illustration of juking the stats and Goodhart-style metric gaming.

xIraCchPDhk.summary: A four-minute clip of George Carlin arguing that voting is a way of keeping people in a distracted bubble, and that non-voters have as much right to complain as anyone.
xIraCchPDhk.why: Mostly dropped in as a quip or reference in threads about politics and cynicism, not recommended as something to watch.

xJzYRgmnJrE.summary: A 1982 Xerox PARC film, presented at CHI '90, in which Star designers David Canfield Smith and Charles Irby give an overview of the Xerox Star interface. It shows the document-centric, icon-and-window office system.
xJzYRgmnJrE.why: Cited as the primary historical demo of the Star UI whenever its influence on the Mac and Lisa or document-centric design is discussed.

xNzXze5Yza8.summary: A short, ironic Cadillac ELR 2014 commercial celebrating long working hours and the American dream, which has been widely mocked.
xNzXze5Yza8.why: Cited critically as an example of US advertising that glorifies overwork and lack of holiday time.

xO1zxPRRf4g.summary: A three-minute clip from The Wire season 3 in which Stringer Bell chairs a drug-crew business meeting using Robert's Rules of Order. The scene plays the formal procedure against the criminal setting.
xO1zxPRRf4g.why: Linked as a joke or reference whenever Robert's Rules or formal meeting procedure comes up.

xOQmQpKHVWA.summary: CNBC coverage of Boeing CEO Dennis Muilenburg answering shareholder questions after the 737 Max crashes. He assures shareholders the plane is safe after a software fix.
xOQmQpKHVWA.why: Mostly cited critically as an example of a CEO deflecting blame during the 737 Max crisis.

xSVqLHghLpw.summary: A one-minute clip from The Simpsons in which Lisa demonstrates the Anti-Tiger Rock to Homer, showing that the rock keeps away tigers because no tigers are around. It is a short comedic scene about faulty causal reasoning.
xSVqLHghLpw.why: HN commenters post it as a joke whenever a thread involves correlation, causation, or unfalsifiable protective measures.

xU4GdHLUHwU.summary: Short clip of Donald Rumsfeld's 9/10/2001 speech acknowledging that $2.3 trillion in Pentagon transactions could not be tracked.
xU4GdHLUHwU.why: Referenced when commenters discuss unaccounted government money, conspiracy theories, or financial fraud.

xUEob2oAKVs.summary: Project Farm tests six penetrating oils, including WD-40, PB Blaster, Liquid Wrench and an ATF and acetone mix, on rusted bolts. Liquid Wrench placed first and the homemade mix second.
xUEob2oAKVs.why: Cited as a hands-on comparison showing WD-40 is not the best penetrating oil.

xUJtqvYDnkg.summary: LockPickingLawyer examines a challenge involving a tamper-sealed Abus lock and shows how the tamper seal can be defeated.
xUJtqvYDnkg.why: Referenced in security threads as proof that tamper-evident seals and stickers can be bypassed.

xbiDrzTd8fE.summary: A scene from The Big Short in which Jared Vennett pitches credit default swaps on mortgage bonds to a hedge fund team, using a Jenga tower to illustrate collateralized debt obligations.
xbiDrzTd8fE.why: Used as a quick visual explanation of how CDOs packaged risky mortgage debt.

xgy0rW0oaFI.summary: Part 1 of Jean-Marc Jancovici's 2019 course at Ecole des Mines de Paris, on energy and its central role in the economy and climate. It is in French with English subtitles available and runs about two and a half hours.
xgy0rW0oaFI.why: Cited as a source lecture series behind arguments on energy, EROEI, nuclear power and climate.

xnhJWusyj4I.summary: Clip from a John Oliver segment showing Newt Gingrich arguing that feelings about crime matter more than FBI statistics at the 2016 RNC.
xnhJWusyj4I.why: Cited critically as an example of post-truth politics and appeals to feeling over data.

xo9cKe_Fch8.summary: Steve Jobs announces the iPhone App Store at the 2008 iPhone SDK keynote, including the 70/30 revenue split for developers and free apps at no charge.
xo9cKe_Fch8.why: Cited as the primary source for the original App Store terms and Apple's stated reason for the 30% cut.

xoHbn8-ROiQ.summary: A short clip from Swedish magazine Teknikens Värld showing the 2016 Toyota Hilux nearly tipping over during the evasive-maneuver moose test.
xoHbn8-ROiQ.why: HN cites it as evidence of a vehicle stability flaw that Toyota was slow to fix.

xrzMYL901AQ.summary: Fox Business interview in which Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison claims Oracle will beat Amazon at cloud databases. He argues the world's valuable data lives in Oracle and says Amazon struggled to move off it.
xrzMYL901AQ.why: Cited as a source for Ellison's comments about Amazon and Oracle, usually in threads about Amazon migrating off Oracle, and often critically.

xubbVvKbUfY.summary: A KRAZAM comedy sketch in which Makro walks through the latest Microsoft Office 365 Excel update in a mock stream highlights format.
xubbVvKbUfY.why: Posted as a joke or obligatory sketch in threads about Excel, Microsoft products and tech layoffs.

xvFZjo5PgG0.summary: A zero-length alternate-link copy of the Rick Astley 'Never Gonna Give You Up' rickroll, made to avoid ads.
xvFZjo5PgG0.why: Used purely as a rickroll joke link.

xxX81WmXjPg.summary: Stavros Korokithakis gives a FOSDEM 2018 talk on how hard it is to validate email addresses properly, taking a tour through RFC 5321.
xxX81WmXjPg.why: Linked whenever email validation comes up as a fun illustration of how deceptively difficult it is.

xxYmMRxnEic.summary: A scene from John Carpenter's 1981 film Escape from New York in which Snake Plissken glides in over Manhattan between the Twin Towers. It features the film's wireframe green laser-grid visuals built from miniatures.
xxYmMRxnEic.why: HN uses it to illustrate how the film's wireframe skyline effect was made with practical miniatures and as an example of retro computer-display aesthetics.

xxjiQoTp864.summary: A six-minute clip of Adobe's MAX 2011 sneak peek showing a Photoshop prototype that removes motion blur from photos. The audience reacts with astonishment as blurry images become legible.
xxjiQoTp864.why: Linked as a memorable early demo of image deblurring whenever threads on image restoration or synthesis come up.

xyg_v7Vxo4A.summary: A two-minute clip from The Wire in which characters speculate about who invented Chicken McNuggets.
xyg_v7Vxo4A.why: HN uses it as a joke reference in threads about accidental inventors and automating jobs.
